video.title: How to Get Your First Service Clients Paying Tens of Thousands

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Jamison, a former private-equity professional who launched West Coast Decks in Southern California with no trade experience. He closed $60,000 of jobs in month one using paid lead services, and says he reached just under $1M in year one and now does $4-8M a year. The video is a tactical playbook for launching a high-ticket home service business: pick a low-decision-count, high-order-value niche, invest in branding early, respond to leads in seconds, hire a well-paid VA, cultivate referrals from adjacent trades via social media, and bid at 50% gross margin (2x COGS).

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; owns a tree trimming business

speakers.name: Jamison
speakers.description: Founder of West Coast Decks (Southern California), ex-Wall Street/private equity

ideas.name: West Coast Decks (premium deck building)
ideas.one_liner: High-ticket deck design and build company in Southern California, started with no trade experience using strong branding and fast lead response.
ideas.business_model: Per-job project sales, bid at about 2x cost of service (50% gross margin)
ideas.customer: Southern California homeowners wanting new decks or deck repair; also referrals via landscapers, roofers and other trades
ideas.problem: Homeowners want a deck built or repaired by a trustworthy, professional contractor rather than a handyman; the market is short of good providers
ideas.offer: Design and installation of decks (wood or composite, railings, optional lighting and outdoor kitchens), sold in a short one-meeting close

pricing.model: Project-based quote; cost of labor and materials x2
pricing.notes: Early pricing was admittedly too low, which helped close the first jobs and gather social proof.

acquisition_channels.details: Paid lead services at launch (Angie's List, HomeAdvisor; today Thumbtack, TaskRabbit, Angie). Deck repair leads about $60 and deck build leads about $120. Respond within 30 seconds, site visit within a day, proposal within another day.
Posts daily on Instagram and Facebook plus an email newsletter; consistent branding and profiles on Google, Yelp, Houzz, BBB and Chamber of Commerce.

Instagram-driven referrals from other trades (mostly landscapers, roofers) said to produce about $400k in year one and $600k in year two; also meets lumber yards and supplier sales reps in person who send leads.
No ads for the first 3 years; PPC, Google LSA and Meta ads are a 2026 initiative.

ideas.delivery: Installed physically by crews; California in-house versus subcontractors is tricky, he says either works if managed well. Installs about half a million sq ft of decking per year.
unit_economics_claims: Closed $60k in 3 jobs in month one for about $1,500 of lead spend
Bid at 50% gross margin (2x COGS) to reach about 15% net
Year one revenue just under $1M; now $4-8M per year
ideas.startup_cost: $15,000 set aside as working capital; branding under about $3,000
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First month ($60k closed within about 3 days of leads)

acquisition.how: Lead-marketplace purchases, ads and social posting can be tooled, but supplier/trade relationship building and rapid human responses drive results.

onboarding.how: Site visits and quote meetings are in person; design decisions made with the client.

billing.how: Invoicing and deposits can be handled by software, with change-order enforcement by humans.

support.how: Homeowner expectation management needs a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Home-improvement decking works in the UK, but lead platforms differ (Checkatrade, MyBuilder, Bark), the climate and regulations differ, and he would need real trade crews.

risks: Asymmetric downside: costs only compress after the bid
Need to respond instantly to leads

tactics.name: Cheap crowdsourced branding kit
steps: Browse Pinterest, Behance or Dribbble for brands you like, even from other industries
Post an Upwork or Fiverr job: $200 for 20 design concepts, hire about 5 designers (about $1,000, around 100 concepts)
Pick the 3 favourite concepts
Hire a designer for a full kit (logo, typography, colours, uniforms) for $500-750
Total under about $3,000

quote.text: for $200, I want 20 design concepts for my brand
quote.speaker: Jamison

tactics.name: Name = service area + service
steps: Name the business [Place] + [Service], e.g. Dallas Decks
Check the .com is available before committing
Avoid owner-name branding

quote.text: The simple equation for what you name your business is your service area and your service.
quote.speaker: Jamison

tactics.name: Speed to lead
steps: Respond to every lead within 30 seconds (5-minute hard limit)
Do a qualifying call or site visit immediately, site visit within a day
Deliver the proposal within another day
Keep phone ringer on and answer

quote.text: need to respond to a lead within 30 seconds. We have a like a 5-minute rule upon pain of death
quote.speaker: Jamison

tactics.name: Bootstrap social proof
steps: Ask friends, neighbours, former co-workers and online followers for reviews
Set up Google, Yelp, Houzz, BBB, Chamber of Commerce profiles with identical name, phone and address
Use lead-gen platforms to get first jobs and real reviews

tactics.name: Referral ecosystem from adjacent trades and suppliers
steps: Post daily on Instagram and Facebook so roofers, landscapers etc. see your work
Visit lumber yards and supplier sales reps in person and ask how you can help each other
Hire a VA to support the posting and admin

quote.text: they will send you leads. They will send you business.
quote.speaker: Jamison

tactics.name: Price at 2x cost and hold the line
steps: Measure labour and material cost, multiply by 2
Push price as high as possible at the bid stage
Enforce subcontractor agreements, tight labour budgets and supplier terms
Charge for change orders and stick to scope

quote.text: bid at 50% gross, which means 2x your COGS
quote.speaker: Jamison

tactics.name: Overpay your first VA offshore
steps: Pay about $12-15 per hour to a VA in Central/South America or the Philippines rather than the lowest rate
This buys an experienced person who can work without an established system

quote.text: pay 12 or 15, which feels like a lot
quote.speaker: Jamison

warnings.warning: Underpricing early can help close jobs but is a loss leader.
Scaling from about $3M to $8M is a 'death zone' where you need leadership you cannot yet afford.

lessons.lesson: Choose a niche with high average order value and few client decisions to reduce room for error.

quote.text: the ratio of average order value to number of decisions that the client needs to make reduces the opportunity to screw things up
quote.speaker: Jamison

lessons.lesson: Professional branding early can substitute for missing track record when trust matters.
Speed of response is the most important sales advantage in local services.
Use paid lead marketplaces to get first jobs and reviews, then shift to organic referral and later paid ads.
Price at 2x cost; confusing margin and markup is common and fatal.
Targeting adjacent trades and suppliers for referrals is cheap and compounding.
Going all-in with commitment (contractual obligations, burned boats) drove execution.
Well-run trade businesses should net about 15%; more suggests underinvestment, less suggests a problem.
Key-man risk persists until a management team exists, typically around $7-8M revenue.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with a detailed playbook and plausible numbers, but revenue figures are approximate and unverified, and the guest was imprecise about year one and profit.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor read for GoHighLevel and plug for TK Owners community; guest invites inbound contact for his deck business and hiring.
